(the month-two trap)

lines.text: 84% of people who budget have blown it. Here's why.
lines.say: Eighty-four percent of people who budget have blown it. Here's why.

lines.text: That's from a 2023 NerdWallet survey of people with a monthly budget. And the trap often shows up in month two.
lines.say: That's from a twenty twenty-three NerdWallet survey of people with a monthly budget. And the trap often shows up in month two.

scene.label: Budgeters who've gone over at some point

lines.text: Month one is easy: you plan around the bills you just paid.
lines.say: Month one is easy: you plan around the bills you just paid.

lines.text: Then come the ones you forgot: renewals, gifts, repairs, and registration fees.
lines.say: Then come the ones you forgot: renewals, gifts, repairs, and registration fees.

lines.text: They're not emergencies. They're just not monthly.

lines.text: Say yours add up to $2,400 a year: gifts, an insurance renewal, car repairs, and Prime at $139.
lines.say: Say yours add up to twenty-four hundred dollars a year: gifts, an insurance renewal, car repairs, and Prime at one thirty-nine.

lines.text: Divide by 12, and that's $200 a month. Planners call it a sinking fund.
lines.say: Divide by twelve, and that's two hundred dollars a month. Planners call it a sinking fund.

lines.text: Costs creep, too. Average household spending rose from $63,036 in 2019 to $78,535 in 2024.

lines.text: The takeaway: plan the year, then divide by 12.

post.title: 84% of people who budget have blown it. Here's the month-two trap.
post.ig:
84% of people who budget have blown it. Here's why.
In a 2023 NerdWallet survey, 84% of people with a monthly budget said they'd gone over it, and the trap often shows up in month two.
Month one is built on bills you know. Month two brings the irregular ones: renewals, gifts, repairs.
Example: $2,400 a year of irregular costs / 12 = $200 a month.
Sources: NerdWallet/Harris Poll (2023); BLS Consumer Expenditure Survey (2024).
News and education, not financial advice.
